title: Four Rules Heat Must Obey
question: What four rules govern heat, energy and entropy?
hook: Every machine ever imagined that runs forever breaks at least one of them.
idea: Four laws define temperature, conserve energy, give heat a one-way direction, and fix entropy near absolute zero.

beats.prompt: match each law to what it says
pairs: Energy is conserved, never created or destroyed
Entropy of interacting systems never decreases
Entropy approaches a constant near absolute zero
beats.explain: Each law covers a different quantity: temperature, energy, entropy and its behavior at the coldest limit.

beats.prompt: An inventor says a ship can scoop heat out of the ocean and turn all of it into propulsion, with no energy lost or made. What does thermodynamics say?

choices.label: It works, since no energy is created
choices.feedback: It tempts because the energy books balance, but balancing energy is only the first law's demand.

choices.label: It fails, since heat cannot spontaneously be turned into work
It works if the ocean is warm enough
choices.feedback: It tempts because warmer water holds more heat, but the problem is the conversion, not the amount.

choices.label: It fails, since the ship would create energy
choices.feedback: It tempts because perpetual motion sounds like free energy, but this ship takes its energy from the ocean.

beats.explain: This is a perpetual motion machine of the second kind. The first law is satisfied, but the second law forbids spontaneously converting thermal energy into mechanical work.

beats.prompt: sort each claim by the law it breaks
items: A machine makes work with no energy input
Energy appears from nothing in an isolated box
Heat flows by itself from ice to a warm room
A drink warms itself by pulling heat from cold air
beats.explain: The first law forbids creating energy; the second forbids heat moving from colder to warmer by itself.

beats.prompt: put these milestones in the order they happened
items: Carnot's principle, the seed of the second law (1824)
Nernst's theorem, now the third law (1906 to 1912)
beats.explain: The laws were not found in numerical order: the zeroth, the most basic, was named last.
